code: # Example with raw data with method "Bartlett" EFA_raw <- efa_fit(DOSPERT_raw, n_factors = 10, method = "PAF",                    rotation = "oblimin",                    rotate_control = rotate_control(random_starts = 1)) #> ℹ `x` is not a correlation matrix; computing correlations from the raw data. fac_scores_raw <- FACTOR_SCORES(DOSPERT_raw, f = EFA_raw, method = "Bartlett")  # Same as above, but with raw data AND a correlation matrix cor_pearson <- cor(DOSPERT_raw) EFA_cor_pearson <- efa_fit(cor_pearson, n_factors = 10, N = nrow(DOSPERT_raw),                            method = "PAF", rotation = "oblimin",                            rotate_control = rotate_control(random_starts = 1)) fac_scores_cor_pearson <- FACTOR_SCORES(DOSPERT_raw, f = EFA_cor_pearson,                                         rho = cor_pearson,                                         method = "Bartlett")  # Scores between two alternatives above are identical isTRUE(all.equal(fac_scores_raw$scores, fac_scores_cor_pearson$scores,                  check.attributes = FALSE)) #> [1] TRUE  # Example with a correlation matrix only (does not return factor scores) EFA_cor <- efa_fit(test_models$baseline$cormat, n_factors = 3, N = 500,                    method = "PAF", rotation = "oblimin") fac_scores_cor <- FACTOR_SCORES(test_models$baseline$cormat, f = EFA_cor) #> ℹ `x` is a correlation matrix; factor scores cannot be computed. Only factor #>   weights and score diagnostics are returned. Enter raw data to get factor #>   scores.

code: # \donttest{ ## Use with lavaan outputs if (requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)) {  # Create and fit bifactor model in lavaan (assume all variables have SDs of 1) mod <- 'F1 =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5 + V6         F2 =~ V7 + V8 + V9 + V10 + V11 + V12         F3 =~ V13 + V14 + V15 + V16 + V17 + V18         g =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5 + V6 + V7 + V8 + V9 + V10 + V11 + V12 +              V13 + V14 + V15 + V16 + V17 + V18' fit_bi <- lavaan::cfa(mod, sample.cov = test_models$baseline$cormat,                       sample.nobs = 500, estimator = "ml", orthogonal = TRUE)  # Compute omegas and additional indices for bifactor solution OMEGA(fit_bi, g_name = "g")  # Compute only omegas OMEGA(fit_bi, g_name = "g", add_ind = FALSE)  # Create and fit second-order model in lavaan (assume all variables have SDs of 1) mod <- 'F1 =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5 + V6         F2 =~ V7 + V8 + V9 + V10 + V11 + V12         F3 =~ V13 + V14 + V15 + V16 + V17 + V18         g =~ F1 + F2 + F3' fit_ho <- lavaan::cfa(mod, sample.cov = test_models$baseline$cormat,                       sample.nobs = 500, estimator = "ml")  # Compute omegas and additional indices for second-order solution OMEGA(fit_ho, g_name = "g") } #> ℹ The specified general factor is a second-order factor; omegas are computed on #>   the Schmid-Leiman transformed second-order solution. #> Omega total, omega hierarchical, omega subscale, H index, explained common #> variance (ECV), and percent of uncontaminated correlations (PUC) for the #> general factor (top row) and omegas and H index for the group factors: #>  #>      tot  hier   sub     H   ECV   PUC #> g  0.882 0.764 0.118 0.848 0.684 0.706 #> F1 0.744 0.549 0.195 0.361             #> F2 0.764 0.504 0.259 0.448             #> F3 0.768 0.505 0.263 0.454             # }  ## Use with an output from the SL function, with type EFAtools efa_mod <- efa_fit(test_models$baseline$cormat, N = 500, n_factors = 3,                    method = "PAF", rotation = "promax") sl_mod <- efa_schmid_leiman(efa_mod, method = "PAF")  # Two examples how to specify the indicator-to-factor correspondences:  # Based on a specific salience threshold for the loadings (here: .20): factor_corres_1 <- sl_mod$sl[, c("F1", "F2", "F3")] >= .2  # Or more flexibly (could also be TRUE and FALSE instead of 0 and 1): factor_corres_2 <- matrix(c(rep(0, 12), rep(1, 6), rep(0, 6), rep(1, 6),                          rep(0, 6), rep(1, 6), rep(0, 12)), ncol = 3,                          byrow = FALSE)  OMEGA(sl_mod, type = "EFAtools", factor_corres = factor_corres_1) #> Omega total, omega hierarchical, omega subscale, H index, explained common #> variance (ECV), and percent of uncontaminated correlations (PUC) for the #> general factor (top row) and omegas and H index for the group factors: #>  #>      tot  hier   sub     H   ECV   PUC #> g  0.883 0.740 0.125 0.842 0.652 0.706 #> F1 0.769 0.500 0.269 0.463             #> F2 0.763 0.494 0.270 0.472             #> F3 0.744 0.519 0.225 0.408              ## Use with an output from the psych::schmid function, with type psych for ## OMEGA schmid_mod <- psych::schmid(test_models$baseline$cormat, nfactors = 3,                             n.obs = 500, fm = "pa", rotate = "Promax") #> Loading required namespace: GPArotation # Find correlation matrix from phi and pattern matrix from psych::schmid output OMEGA(schmid_mod, type = "psych") #> Omega total, omega hierarchical, omega subscale, H index, explained common #> variance (ECV), and percent of uncontaminated correlations (PUC) for the #> general factor (top row) and omegas and H index for the group factors: #>  #>       tot  hier   sub     H   ECV   PUC #> g   0.883 0.750 0.122 0.845 0.661 0.706 #> F1* 0.769 0.498 0.272 0.466             #> F2* 0.765 0.494 0.271 0.473             #> F3* 0.745 0.543 0.202 0.379             # Use specified correlation matrix OMEGA(schmid_mod, type = "psych", cormat = test_models$baseline$cormat) #> Omega total, omega hierarchical, omega subscale, H index, explained common #> variance (ECV), and percent of uncontaminated correlations (PUC) for the #> general factor (top row) and omegas and H index for the group factors: #>  #>       tot  hier   sub     H   ECV   PUC #> g   0.883 0.750 0.122 0.845 0.661 0.706 #> F1* 0.769 0.498 0.272 0.466             #> F2* 0.764 0.494 0.270 0.473             #> F3* 0.745 0.543 0.202 0.379              ## Manually specify components (useful if omegas should be computed for a SL ## or bifactor solution found with another program) ## As an example, we extract the elements from an SL output here. This gives ## the same results as in the second example above.  efa_mod <- efa_fit(test_models$baseline$cormat, N = 500, n_factors = 3,                    method = "PAF", rotation = "promax") sl_mod <- efa_schmid_leiman(efa_mod, method = "PAF")  factor_corres <- matrix(c(rep(0, 12), rep(1, 6), rep(0, 6), rep(1, 6),                         rep(0, 6), rep(1, 6), rep(0, 12)), ncol = 3,                         byrow = FALSE)  OMEGA(model = NULL, type = "EFAtools", var_names = rownames(sl_mod$sl),       g_load = sl_mod$sl[, "g"], s_load = sl_mod$sl[, c("F1", "F2", "F3")],       u2 = sl_mod$sl[, "u2"], cormat = test_models$baseline$cormat,       factor_corres = factor_corres) #> Omega total, omega hierarchical, omega subscale, H index, explained common #> variance (ECV), and percent of uncontaminated correlations (PUC) for the #> general factor (top row) and omegas and H index for the group factors: #>  #>     tot  hier   sub     H   ECV   PUC #> g 0.883 0.740 0.125 0.842 0.652 0.706 #> 1 0.769 0.500 0.269 0.463             #> 2 0.763 0.494 0.270 0.472             #> 3 0.744 0.519 0.225 0.408

title: Bartlett's test of sphericity — efa_bartlett
text: Bartlett (1951) proposed statistic determine correlation matrix' suitability factor analysis. statistic approximately chi square distributed \(df = \frac{p(p - 1)}{2}\) given $$chi^2 = -log(det(R)) (N - 1 - (2 * p + 5)/6)$$ \(det(R)\) determinant correlation matrix, \(N\) sample size, \(p\) number variables. tests requires multivariate normality. condition met, Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin criterion (efa_kmo()) can still used. function heavily influenced psych::cortest.bartlett() function psych package. efa_bartlett function can also called together (efa_kmo()) function factor retention criteria efa_retain() function.

title: Velicer's minimum average partial (MAP) criterion — efa_map
text: MAP partials successive principal components correlation matrix , removing \(m\) components, summarizes -diagonal partial correlations \(r^*_{ij}\) remain \(m\)-th partial correlation matrix \(M\) (unit diagonal); suggested number factors \(m\) minimizes criterion. Two criteria returned, rescaling trace matrix power \(M\) number -diagonal cells \(p(p-1)\): TR2 (original MAP; Velicer, 1976): average squared -diagonal partial correlation, $$\mathrm{TR2}_m = \frac{\mathrm{tr}(M^2) - p}{p(p-1)} = \frac{\sum_{\neq j} (r^*_{ij})^2}{p(p-1)},$$ subtracting \(p\) removes \(p\) unit diagonal entries. TR4 (revised MAP; Velicer, Eaton, & Fava, 2000): analogous fourth-power summary, formed trace fourth matrix power, $$\mathrm{TR4}_m = \frac{\mathrm{tr}(M^4) - p}{p(p-1)}.$$ Moving squared fourth power downweights small partial correlations relative large ones, can sharpen minimum. non-positive-definite input correlation matrix (e.g. sampling error) smoothed psych::cor.smooth().

title: Schmid-Leiman transformation — efa_schmid_leiman
text: SL transformation (also called SL orthogonalization) procedure oblique factor solution transformed hierarchical, orthogonalized solution. first step, factor intercorrelations factor analyzed extract single second-order (general) factor, yielding two-level hierarchical structure. first-order factor second-order factor orthogonalized, resulting orthogonalized factor solution proportionality constraints. procedure thus makes suggested hierarchical data structure based factor intercorrelations explicit. One major advantage SL transformation enables variance partitioning higher-order first-order factors, including calculation McDonald's omegas (see efa_reliability()).

title: Schmid-Leiman transformation — efa_schmid_leiman
code: ## Use with an output from the EFAtools::efa_fit function, both with type EFAtools EFA_mod <- efa_fit(test_models$baseline$cormat, N = 500, n_factors = 3,                    method = "PAF", rotation = "promax") SL_EFAtools <- efa_schmid_leiman(EFA_mod, method = "PAF",                                  estimate_control = estimate_control(type = "EFAtools"))  # \donttest{ ## Use with an output from the psych::fa function with type psych fa_mod <- psych::fa(test_models$baseline$cormat, nfactors = 3, n.obs = 500,                     fm = "pa", rotate = "Promax") SL_psych <- efa_schmid_leiman(fa_mod, method = "PAF",                               estimate_control = estimate_control(type = "psych")) # }  ## Use more flexibly by entering a pattern matrix and phi directly (useful if ## a factor solution found with another program should be subjected to SL ## transformation)  ## For demonstration, take pattern matrix and phi from an EFA output ## This gives the same solution as the first example EFA_mod <- efa_fit(test_models$baseline$cormat, N = 500, n_factors = 3,                    method = "PAF", rotation = "promax") SL_flex <- efa_schmid_leiman(EFA_mod$rot_loadings, Phi = EFA_mod$Phi, method = "PAF",                              estimate_control = estimate_control(type = "EFAtools"))  # \donttest{ ## Use with a lavaan second-order CFA output if (requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)) {  # Create and fit model in lavaan (assume all variables have SDs of 1) mod <- 'F1 =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5 + V6         F2 =~ V7 + V8 + V9 + V10 + V11 + V12         F3 =~ V13 + V14 + V15 + V16 + V17 + V18         g =~ F1 + F2 + F3' fit <- lavaan::cfa(mod, sample.cov = test_models$baseline$cormat,                    sample.nobs = 500, estimator = "ml")  SL_lav <- efa_schmid_leiman(fit, g_name = "g")  } # }

code: # Build a population from a shipped loading pattern and factor correlations Lambda <- population_models$loadings$baseline Phi <- population_models$phis_3$moderate  # Draw one normal dataset of 500 cases (the data live in $data) sim <- efa_simulate(N = 500, Lambda = Lambda, Phi = Phi, seed = 42) dim(sim$data) #> [1] 500  18  # Return only the population correlation matrix R_pop <- efa_simulate(Lambda = Lambda, Phi = Phi, return_pop = TRUE)$population  # Draw several datasets at once from a supplied correlation matrix sims <- efa_simulate(N = 500, R = R_pop, n_datasets = 3, seed = 42) length(sims$data) #> [1] 3  # Reproduce the population correlation but with skewed, empirical marginals # (here from a chi-squared source with one column per variable) src <- matrix(rchisq(200 * nrow(Lambda), df = 3), ncol = nrow(Lambda)) dat_emp <- efa_simulate(N = 500, Lambda = Lambda, Phi = Phi,                         marginals = "empirical", marginal_data = src, seed = 42)  # Draw skewed, leptokurtic data with the Vale-Maurelli method dat_vm <- efa_simulate(N = 500, Lambda = Lambda, Phi = Phi, marginals = "VM",                        skewness = 1.5, kurtosis = 4, seed = 42)  # Draw five-category ordinal data whose polychoric correlation matches R dat_ord <- efa_simulate(N = 500, Lambda = Lambda, Phi = Phi,                         categories = 5, match = "polychoric", seed = 42)  # Draw data with 15% missing at random, driven by a neighbouring item dat_mar <- efa_simulate(N = 500, Lambda = Lambda, Phi = Phi, missing = "MAR",                         missing_prop = 0.15, seed = 42) colMeans(is.na(dat_mar$data)) #>    V1    V2    V3    V4    V5    V6    V7    V8    V9   V10   V11   V12   V13  #> 0.154 0.146 0.184 0.156 0.152 0.170 0.174 0.138 0.132 0.138 0.128 0.134 0.136  #>   V14   V15   V16   V17   V18  #> 0.132 0.152 0.144 0.166 0.140   # Add realistic model error: a population the model fits with RMSEA of about .05 # (Cudeck-Browne, the default method; the achieved fit is reported) sim_me <- efa_simulate(N = 500, Lambda = Lambda, Phi = Phi,                        target_rmsea = 0.05, seed = 42) sim_me$model_error$rmsea #> [1] 0.04999999

title: EFAtools 0.8.0
text: gains cor_method = "fiml" raw data missing values. gains se = "sandwich" se = "information". renamed top-level fields boot.SE, boot.CI, boot.arrays EFA objects SE, CI, replicates, old names longer accurate given additional SE implementations. criterion-based rotations now computed built-gradient-projection rotation engine instead GPArotation package. rotated solutions numerically equivalent implemented C++ speed allow high numbers random starts. default number random starts rotation EFA() (randomStarts) raised 10 100, making local minima less likely rotation criteria prone . additionally reports Tucker-Lewis index (TLI, also called non-normed fit index), expected cross-validation index (ECVI), standardized root mean square residual (SRMR) gains seed argument now fits non-parametric bootstrap replicates (se = "np-boot") parallel across replicates via future framework. now summary() method prints full, detailed solution (loadings communalities uniquenesses, explained variances, fit indices, residuals); print() now gives compact overview. EFA_AVERAGE() gains cor_method = "fiml" (passed EFA()). now dispatches multiple-imputation standard-error pooling automatically standard-error method component fits: Rubin’s rules information method (Wald confidence intervals), two-stage pooled-inputs (MI2S) approach sandwich method, existing bootstrap pooling non-parametric bootstrap method. Renamed top-level field boot.MI MI. now defaults target_method = "first_target", aligns every imputation first imputation’s rotated solution single Procrustes rotation. orthogonal rotations reaches pooled estimate "consensus" substantially less work. "consensus" (Generalized Procrustes Analysis imputation-specific rotated loadings) still available opt-orthogonal rotations, now raises classed condition (efa_consensus_oblique_unsupported) combined oblique rotation, iterated-oblique-Procrustes centroid can drift degenerate targets. cor_method now accepts "poly" "tetra" compute polychoric tetrachoric correlations raw ordinal (respectively binary) data, using two-step estimator empty-cell continuity correction. Supported EFA() (including non-parametric bootstrap), EFA_AVERAGE(), suitability tests KMO() BARTLETT(), retention criteria EKC(), KGC(), MAP(), SCREE(), SMT(), N_FACTORS(). criteria compare data simulated continuous reference data (CD(), PARALLEL(), NEST(), HULL()) support "poly" / "tetra" signal error. factor-retention functions CD(), EKC(), HULL(), KGC(), MAP(), NEST(), PARALLEL(), SCREE(), SMT() now return objects common efa_retention class shared print() plot() methods. COMPARE() objects now plot() method returns ggplot object. plot longer drawn side effect print(). Console output (print, summary, format methods) now produced cli package, messages, warnings, errors emitted across package now S3-classed conditions, makes easier handle programmatically. EFA(), SL(), EFA_AVERAGE() now accept method = "MINRES" synonym method = "ULS". Minimum residual unweighted least squares two names estimator return identical results.

title: EFAtools 0.8.0
text: EFA() EFA_POOLED(): comparative fit index (CFI) now floors model baseline noncentralities zero taking ratio (Bentler, 1990), longer deflated toward zero baseline (independence) model fits comparatively well. value unchanged well-fitting models now matches lavaan. CFI can change solutions baseline model misfit much. EFA_POOLED(): Corrected extended pooled chi-square-based model-fit indices. D2 average relative increase variance now centred mean square-root statistics (Li, Meng, Raghunathan & Rubin, 1991), removing one-sided inflation pooled chi-square, RMSEA, CFI. Bootstrap/MI confidence intervals pooled fit indices now Rubin-Wald multiple-imputation summaries; miscalibrated bootstrap-percentile interval (obtained re-running pooling algorithm matched replicate indices) removed, mislabeled pooled Fm. EFA_AVERAGE(): every averaged solution fails (runs error, fail converge, Heywood cases), function now returns empty (NA) averaged result instead erroring averaging empty set. EFA() method = "PAF": reported number iterations (iter) now number iterations actually performed; previously one high. loadings, communalities, convergence status unchanged. ULS extraction: minimised objective now sum squared -diagonal residuals, consistent analytic gradient reported minimum (Fm). diagonal residuals previously included objective gradient. fitted loadings unchanged within optimiser tolerance. NEST() PARALLEL(): failed eigendecomposition degenerate simulated matrix now raises clear error instead resulting undefined behaviour. chi-square model-fit statistic now Bartlett-corrected maximum likelihood discrepancy evaluated model-implied correlation matrix, ML ULS extraction. method = "ML" matches stats::factanal() psych::fa(); small-sample Bartlett correction previously omitted. method = "ULS" now proper chi-square-distributed statistic matching psych::fa(fm = "minres"); previously least-squares residual sum squares multiplied N - 1 read Wishart-distributed, produced invalid p-value. independence (baseline) model used CFI rescaled onto discrepancy scale. Consequently p-value, CFI, RMSEA (confidence interval), AIC, BIC change ML ULS solutions, number factors suggested SMT() HULL() may change methods. PARALLEL(): percentile reference eigenvalues now computed stats::quantile(), correcting slight --one previous indexing. EFA(): oblique rotations, factor intercorrelations (Phi), structure matrix, explained variances now reflected reordered consistently rotated loadings. Previously, factor reflected positive orientation factor intercorrelations sign-adjusted (structure matrix reported correlations match loadings), order_type = "ss_factors" factor intercorrelations reordered . EFA(): returned rotation matrix (rotmat) now reflected reordered consistently rotated loadings, orthogonal oblique rotations, rotated loadings can reconstructed unrotated loadings rotmat. Previously sign reflection applied factors left different order, reconstruction hold whenever factor reflected reordered. HULL(): convex-hull elimination now tests every triplet adjacent solutions, including one formed last interior solution. Previously final triplet skipped, solution lying line connecting neighbours remain hull. can change number factors suggested HULL() (hence N_FACTORS()). NEST(): test accepts every eigenvalue examines (empirical eigenvalue falls reference within search range), now retains last accepted model rather model one fewer factor. search range also bounded reference model fitted step stays -identified. PARALLEL(): every real eigenvalue exceeds reference, decision rule finds crossing, suggested number factors now retained components, reported warning, instead silent NA (matching convention used EKC()). EFA(se = "np-boot"): non-parametric bootstrap longer repeats per-replicate warnings (arguments pinned alongside type, iterative fit reaching maximum number iterations) per replicate. now suppressed resampling, non-convergence across replicates reported summary. COMPARE(): reorder = "congruence", columns y now matched x optimal one--one assignment maximizes total Tucker congruence, rather independent per-factor best match. greedy match assign two factors x column y, duplicating column dropping another, corrupted reported differences, factor correspondences, root mean squared distance. result unchanged whenever greedy match already one--one.
